title: Chicken Biryani
subtitle: Fragrant layered rice and chicken with saffron and fresh herbs
excerpt: Biryani is a celebration dish: layers of spiced chicken and partially cooked basmati rice sealed together so the steam finishes both at once. Saffron bloomed in warm milk gives the top layer its golden colour. This version uses the stovetop dum method, which produces reliably good results without a specialist oven.
sourceNotes: Biryani is thought to have arrived in India via Persian traders and Mughal court kitchens, with the word derived from the Persian birian, meaning fried before cooking. Regional variations span from Hyderabadi to Lucknawi to Kolkata styles.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chicken can be marinated overnight. Cook and assemble on the day of serving.

content.text: Rinsing the rice until the water runs clear removes excess starch and keeps the grains separate. Do not skip this step.

items.prepNote: rinsed until the water runs clear

content.text: Steep the saffron in the warm milk and set aside. Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, garlic, ginger, cinnamon, cardamom, and a generous pinch of salt. Leave to marinate for at least 1 hour.
Fry the sliced onion in the ghee over medium-high heat until deep golden and beginning to crisp, around 15 minutes. Remove half the onion and set aside for the topping.
Add the marinated chicken to the pan with the remaining onion. Cook, stirring, for 10 minutes until the chicken is sealed and the yoghurt has dried down.

Meanwhile, bring the large saucepan of salted water to the boil with the cloves, cumin seeds, and bay leaves. Add the rinsed rice and boil for 6 minutes until the rice is just parboiled with a firm core. Drain well.

Layer the parboiled rice over the chicken in the pan, scatter over the mint and coriander, then pour the saffron milk over the top. Scatter the reserved crispy onion over everything. Cover the pan tightly with foil then the lid. Cook over the lowest possible heat for 25 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from the heat and leave to rest for 5 minutes before lifting the lid. Gently fold the layers together from the side before serving.

items.symptom: The rice at the bottom has scorched
items.cause: The heat was too high during the dum (sealed steam) stage
items.fix: Use a heat diffuser or place a folded tea towel between the pan and the lid to help regulate heat next time.

items.symptom: The rice is undercooked in the centre
items.cause: The parboil was too short, or the dum stage was cut short
items.fix: Seal the lid again and continue on low heat for another 10 minutes. The steam trapped inside will finish the rice.
